Rasulullaah ﷺ was Never Rude, Noisy, Vulgar or one who Cursed

Hadhrat Abu Abdullaah Jadali says that when Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was questioned about the character of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he heard her reply, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was never rude and vulgar and never even pretended to be so. He was never noisy in the marketplaces and never fought evil with evil. In fact, he always forgave and overlooked."[^2]

Hadhrat Saalih narrates that when describing Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) said, "When he turned towards someone, he turned completely and when he turned away from someone, he also turned completely. May my parents be sacrificed for him! Rasulullaah ﷺ was never rude and vulgar and never even pretended to be so. He was never noisy in the marketplaces." Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) added, "Never have I seen any like him before and never after."[^3]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was never vulgar, never cursed people and never rude. The most he would tell someone when scolding him was, "What is the matter with him? May sand fall on his forehead!"[^4]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was never rude and vulgar and never even pretended to be so. He always said, 'The best of you is the one with the best character.'"[^5]
Rasulullaah ﷺ's Sterling Character with his Servant Hadhrat Anas (RA)

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, Abu Talha (RA) led me by my hand to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Anas is an intelligent lad. Do let him serve you.' I therefore remained Rasulullaah ﷺ's servant at home and on journey. I swear by Allaah that for anything I did, he never said, 'Why did you do that in that way?' and when I failed to do something, he never once asked, 'Why did you not do that like this?'"[^6]
